content_metadata.description: This video provides a comprehensive guide on adding refrigerant to an AC unit, covering the necessary steps from initial checks to achieving subcooling. It is a part of an HVAC troubleshooting series.

qAndA.answer: The ideal temperature split should be around 18 to 22 degrees Fahrenheit.
qAndA.question: What is the ideal temperature split for a residential AC system?

qAndA.answer: Using a scale ensures accurate measurement of the refrigerant being added, preventing overcharging or undercharging the system.
qAndA.question: Why is it important to use a scale when charging refrigerant?

qAndA.answer: Subcooling is the difference between the high-side saturation temperature and the actual liquid line temperature. It is achieved by gradually adding refrigerant until the desired temperature difference is reached.
qAndA.question: What is subcooling, and how do you achieve it?

qAndA.answer: "Beer can cold" describes the sensation of the suction line being cold to the touch. While a cold suction line can be a sign of proper refrigerant levels, it is not a definitive measure and can be misleading.
qAndA.question: What does the 'beer can cold' term refer to, and why is it not a reliable indicator for refrigerant charge?

qAndA.answer: By using an amp clamp to measure the compressor's current draw. The amp draw should be around 60% of the rated load amperage (RLA) for a healthy compressor.
qAndA.question: How can you monitor the compressor's health during the refrigerant charging process?

youtube_description:
Hey HVAC techs! Since so many other YouTube techs show you how to add refrigerant to an air conditioning system, in this video I thought I'd show you how I add refrigerant to an AC.

I wanted to expand on our recent AC troubleshooting series by going into each part of its sequence of operations.  This week, we're going to talk about how I add refrigerant to an A/C system. How do you get to the point where the air coming out of the registers isn't cold?  You need to add Freon R-22 or Puron R410 refrigerant to your air conditioning system if the temperature difference between the return air and the supply air coming out of the registers is low.  We want this temperature split to be between 18 and 22 degrees.  Ideally, a 20-degree split would be perfect.  But to get there you'll need to add refrigerant by using refrigerant gauges and a digital scale in order to put in the right amount.

Watch this video to get a better grasp on recharging your HVAC system and get your subcooling to the right level.  Charge the 410a or r22 refrigerant the right way, and you won't be in the situation where your AC doesn't cool enough.  Because if your air conditioner is not cooling, it can be tough to stay comfortable on a hot summer day.  I hope you get something out of this video.
